title: YouTube Thumbnail Size: 1280×720 px, 16:9 & File Limits
description: The right YouTube thumbnail size: 1280×720 px works for most uploads, 3840×2160 px is the maximum recommended. Aspect ratio, file limits, Shorts and safe area.
summary: Make a 16:9 image, 1280×720 px or larger, as a JPG or PNG. YouTube recommends up to 3840×2160 px, requires a width of at least 640 px for videos, and limits file size to 2 MB when you upload from a phone and 50 MB from a computer.

sections.heading: YouTube thumbnail specs at a glance
paragraphs: These are the values YouTube lists on its help page for custom thumbnails. They apply to standard, horizontal videos.

rows: 2 MB from the YouTube mobile app, 50 MB from a computer

after: The thumbnail also serves as the preview image in the embedded player, which is why YouTube asks for an image that is as large as possible.

sections.heading: Which size should you export?
paragraphs: For most channels, 1280×720 px is the sensible choice. It has the 16:9 shape YouTube wants, it is sharp on phones and laptops, and a JPG at that size stays far below the 2 MB limit, so you can upload it from any device.

Choose a larger file when your audience watches on big screens or you want the embedded player preview to stay crisp. A 1920×1080 px or 3840×2160 px file is fine, but check the file weight. Detailed images can pass 2 MB quickly, and then you can only upload them from a computer.
Never export below 1280×720 px just to save space. A small image is stretched on large screens and looks soft, and text is the first thing to suffer.

sections.heading: Thumbnail sizes for Shorts and podcasts
paragraphs: Other formats have their own shape. Use the one that matches where the content appears.

rows: Custom Shorts thumbnails are added in YouTube Studio on a computer

after: YouTube notes that a vertical video with a 16:9 custom thumbnail gets an auto-generated 4:5 thumbnail on the home, explore and subscription pages. If most of your viewers watch on a phone, plan for that crop.

sections.heading: Where YouTube covers your thumbnail
paragraphs: YouTube places the video length in the bottom-right corner of the thumbnail in most views. Keep text and faces out of that corner or the badge will cover them. The same corner is a good place for nothing important at all.

Thumbnails also appear very small in suggested videos and on phones. Look at your design at a fraction of its size before you upload. If the headline cannot be read at that size, shorten it or make it larger.
items: Keep the headline to a few words and place it away from the bottom-right corner.
Use strong contrast between the text and the background.
Leave a margin around the edges so nothing is trimmed on small screens.

sections.heading: Common upload problems
items: The file is rejected on mobile: the image is over 2 MB. Export a smaller JPG or upload from a computer, where the limit is 50 MB.
The upload option is missing: custom thumbnails need a verified YouTube account.
Black bars appear: the image is not 16:9. Crop or recreate it at 1280×720 px.
The image looks blurry: it was smaller than 1280×720 px or was saved with heavy compression.
The thumbnail is removed or rejected: it breaks the Community Guidelines, for example by showing nudity, violence or hate speech.
after: There is also a daily limit on custom thumbnails per channel. If you see a "Daily custom thumbnail limit reached" error, try again after 24 hours.

sections.heading: Make a thumbnail at the right size
paragraphs: The [YouTube Thumbnail Maker](/create/youtube-thumbnail-maker) exports a 1280×720 px JPG that stays under 2 MB, so it uploads from a phone or a computer, plus a 1920×1080 px version for large screens. It keeps text and faces out of the bottom-right corner where YouTube shows the video length.

For tips on text, contrast and composition, read the guide to [YouTube thumbnail best practices](/blog/youtube-thumbnail-best-practices). To test a thumbnail you already have against the size, ratio and file limits above, use the free [image size checker](/tools/image-size-checker).

faq.q: What is the best size for a YouTube thumbnail?
faq.a: 1280×720 px at a 16:9 aspect ratio is the safest everyday choice. YouTube recommends up to 3840×2160 px for the sharpest result, with a minimum width of 640 px.

faq.q: Can I upload a thumbnail that is larger than 2 MB?
faq.a: Yes, from a computer. The limit is 50 MB for uploads from a computer and 2 MB for uploads from the YouTube mobile app.

faq.q: Should a thumbnail be JPG or PNG?
faq.a: Either works. JPG gives smaller files for photos, while PNG keeps flat colors and text edges slightly cleaner but can be heavier. If the file is over 2 MB, switch to JPG.

faq.q: Do I need a verified account to use custom thumbnails?
faq.a: Yes. YouTube only lets verified accounts upload custom thumbnails. Without one you can choose from the suggested frames.

faq.q: What aspect ratio should a Shorts thumbnail have?
faq.a: 9:16, ideally 2160×3840 px with a minimum height of 640 px. Custom Shorts thumbnails can currently be added in YouTube Studio on a computer.

faq.q: Why does my thumbnail look different on my phone?
faq.a: Phones show thumbnails much smaller, the video length badge covers the bottom-right corner, and some views crop the image. Check the design at a small size and keep key elements away from the edges.
